title: Pen-test engagement: stakeholder grid, scope mapping, and evidence flow
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a practical engagement checklist for external penetration tests focusing on RBAC v2, audit-log completeness, and SIEM export/evidence automation. It is intended to standardize communications, streamline evidence packaging, and reduce back-and-forth during validation.

Summary / Why this exists:
- We frequently receive scope questions from assessors about which RBAC objects, control plane APIs, and private deployment components are in scope.
- Assessors need a reproducible, machine-readable evidence bundle for SIEM ingest and our audit export format.
- A lightweight stakeholder grid and clear triage/remediation flow reduce delays and ambiguity.

High-level engagement objectives:
1) Validate RBAC v2 enforcement across control plane and private deployments (role bindings, attribute-based checks, escalation guards).
2) Confirm audit log coverage for privileged actions and important state transitions.
3) Verify SIEM export reliability and schema mapping (ECS/CEF compatibility).
4) Provide assessors with an automated evidence export and a human-friendly index to accelerate findings validation.

In-scope systems and boundaries:
- Control plane API endpoints (admin console, rollout APIs, model pinning APIs): full read/write operations in staging and preprod.
- Dedicated & Private deployment control paths: orchestration APIs, admin consoles, user management endpoints.
- Identity and access systems connected to RBAC v2: IdP (OIDC providers), internal service accounts, role-binding registry, policy engine (authorization service).
- Audit log pipeline: application logs -> audit-transformer -> kafka topic (audit-events) -> SIEM-exporter.

Out-of-scope (examples):
- Customer data stored in third-party backups unless explicitly requested.
- Production-only secrets stores when tests are run against staging; exceptions require legal sign-off.

RBAC v2 specifics to test (mapping to artifacts to collect):
- Role definitions: collect role JSONs (role id, allowed_actions, resource_patterns, constraints).
- Role bindings: all binding manifests showing principal -> role assignments and binding conditions.
- Effective permission check logs: for a given request id, capture authorization decision, policy_version, and predicate evaluation.
- Escalation guard checks: records where a role change was attempted (who, when, outcome, approval token).
- Service account impersonation attempts and successful impersonations.

Audit log schema (canonical fields we expect in audit-events):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- request_id (uuid)
- trace_id (optional, distributed trace id)
- actor_type (user | service | admin)
- actor_id (principal id or service account id)
- actor_email
- client_ip
- action (verb, e.g., role.bind.create, model.rollout.update)
- resource_type (console, model, rollout, role, binding)
- resource_id
- resource_attrs (stringified map summary)
- outcome (allowed | denied | error)
- outcome_reason (policy id or error message)
- prev_state_digest (short hash or version token)
- new_state_digest
- policy_version
- duration_ms
- correlating_artifacts (list of related request_ids)
- raw_payload_reference (s3:// or blob id)

Sample audit-event (compact JSON string form for reviewers):
{"timestamp":"2024-10-01T14:22:31Z","request_id":"6f8d4c3a-1b2e-4aef-a7a1-9d0b3f1f2c4b","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"u-10234","actor_email":"eng-ops@redwood.ai","client_ip":"198.51.100.34","action":"role.binding.create","resource_type":"binding","resource_id":"b-993","outcome":"allowed","policy_version":"rbac-v2-2024-09-18","prev_state_digest":"","new_state_digest":"d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"}

SIEM export guidance and mappings:
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON with gzip compression. Each event must include a top-level ecs_compatible map.
- Required field mappings:
  - audit.timestamp -> @timestamp (ECS)
  - audit.actor_email -> user.email
  - audit.client_ip -> source.ip
  - audit.action -> event.action
  - audit.outcome -> event.outcome
  - audit.request_id -> event.id
  - audit.trace_id -> trace.id
  - raw_payload_reference -> file.hash or url for evidence linkage
- Splunk hints: add sourcetype: "redwood:audit:event" and add the request_id to the event_id field for fast lookup.
- ElasticSearch hints: index alias "audit-events-YYYY.MM" and include dataset: "redwood.audit" for dashboards.

Evidence automation and packaging (recommended minimal bundle):
- Automated export job (preprod-export-pt-<engagement-id>) produces a tar.gz that contains:
  - events-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz (filtered by engagement window and scope)
  - manifest.json (engagement_id, time_range, export_version, sha256 of files)
  - sample-requests/ folder with up to 25 raw request payloads referenced by events
  - rbacs/ folder containing role definitions and binding manifests (redacted where necessary)
  - validation-report.txt (count of events, first/last timestamps, missing-fields summary)
- Packaging rules: manifest fields must be machine-parseable and human-readable. Signed manifest recommended (pgp or HMAC) to avoid tampering during validation.
- Retention for pen-test evidence: keep artifacts in a locked bucket for 180 days (subject to legal).

Stakeholder grid (who does what):
- Engagement Lead (security): Priya Shah — primary point for scope, external communications, evidence sign-off.
- Engineering liaison (Eng: RBAC/Policy): Ethan Lopez — produce role/binding exports, supply policy engine logs, respond to questions about enforcement.
- Observability/SIEM owner: Mina Park — produce SIEM export job, deliver index mapping, provide guidance on ingestion.
- SRE/Infra: Liam O'Connor — enable temporary access to staging clusters, rotate keys post-engagement, ensure export jobs have required IAM.
- Solutions/Cust Success contact (if customer-managed deployment): Sarah Nguyen — coordinate customer approvals and per-customer evidence scoping.

Communication templates (short snippets for assessors):
- Initial scope reply: "Attached is a machine-readable RBAC export and a sample audit-event set covering the requested test window. Please reference request_id field when raising findings to help us locate raw payloads."
- Evidence delivery note: "Bundle signed with HMAC (id: export-20241005-hmac). Manifest includes SHA256 for each file. Reach out to security+evidence@redwood.ai for verification keys."

Triage and remediation flow (recommended quick process):
1) Assessor files finding with request_id and severity suggestion.
2) Security triage (within 24h): validate reproducibility, identify owner.
3) Owner creates JIRA with reproducible steps, links assessor sample request and audit-event.
4) Remediation sprint (target: P1 = 72h hotfix window; P2 = 7d patch; P3 = next minor release).
5) Validation: assessor or internal reviewer confirms that event sequence shows fixed outcome and updated audit-event indicates new policy_version or state change.

Severity guidance (simple):
- P1: privilege escalation or bypasses that allow access to customer data or ability to change RBAC policies without authorization.
- P2: admin UI issues that could lead to confusion or intermittent incorrect logs but not full bypass.
- P3: informational inconsistencies, minor gaps in audit payload fields.

Remediation owner matrix (examples with placeholder JIRA keys):
- Authorization logic bug -> eng-policy -> JIRA-SC-2010 -> owner: Ethan Lopez
- Missing audit fields -> observability -> JIRA-SC-2011 -> owner: Mina Park
- SIEM mapping mismatch -> infra-logs -> JIRA-SC-2012 -> owner: Liam O'Connor

Acceptance criteria for closed findings:
- Repro steps included in JIRA.
- New audit-events for the same request_id show expected outcome and policy_version.
- SIEM dashboard shows no parsing errors for at least 24 hours after deploy (smoke window).
- Evidence bundle updated and re-signed; manifest version bumped.

Quick verification checklist for reviewers:
- [ ] Manifest present and signed
- [ ] events.ndjson.gz decompresses to valid JSON lines with expected fields
- [ ] request_id referenced in finding exists in events set
- [ ] role/binding files exist and match the time window
- [ ] SIEM mapping doc attached (index, dataset, sourcetype)

Post-engagement follow-up:
- Conduct a 1-hour internal lessons-learned within 7 days.
- Update this document with any recurring assessor requests or missing artifacts to reduce friction.
- If new log fields were added, record them in the central audit-schema registry (CONFLUENCE-SEC-AUDITS).

Appendix A: quick commands and hints (operational)
- Export sample (pseudo): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://cp.preprod.redwood.ai/audit/export?from=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&to=2024-10-02T00:00:00Z&engagement=PT-472" | gzip > events-20241001.ndjson.gz
- Verify manifest sha: sha256sum events-20241001.ndjson.gz -> compare with manifest.json
- Minimal jq filter for missing fields: jq -r 'select(.actor_email==null or .action==null) | .request_id' events-*.ndjson

Appendix B: quick mapping cheatsheet (fields -> actionable):
- actor_email -> used for owner lookup and evidence contact
- request_id -> primary key for event correlation and payload retrieval
- policy_version -> important to assert that fix included an updated policy or rule id

Notes / open questions:
- Decide whether manifests should be PGP-signed (preferred for external testers) or HMAC-signed (preferred internally). Security to decide by engineering sign-off.
- Confirm retention policy with legal for any customer-related payloads in evidence bundles.

Document history:
- 2024-10-05: initial draft created by Priya Shah
- 2024-10-08: added SIEM mapping tips (Mina Park)
- 2024-10-12: added remediation owner matrix and sample audit schema (Ethan Lopez)
